title: Linear Graphs: Gradient, Intercepts and y = mx + c
seo_title: Grade 9 Linear Graphs Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Analyse and interpret global graphs of problem situations; draw linear graphs from given equations; determine equations from given linear graphs; extend the focus on features of graphs to include x-intercept and y-intercept and the gradient of a line.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 9 linear graphs worksheets: gradient, intercepts, y = mx + c, parallel lines and global graphs. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • In y = mx + c, m is the gradient and c is the y-intercept.
  • Gradient = change in ychange in x.
  • The x-intercept is where y = 0; the y-intercept is where x = 0.
  • Parallel lines have the same gradient.

Examples

Example

Line through (1; 3) and (4; 9)

m = 6 ÷ 3 = 2

3 = 2 + c

Answer: y = 2x + 1

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
m or c?c is where the line crosses the y-axis.
Upside downChange in y over change in x.
Parallel means same cParallel means same m.

items.q: Find the gradient of the line through (0, 6) and (3, 12).
items.e: Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x = (12 − 6) ÷ (3 − 0) = 6 ÷ 3 = 2.

items.q: Find the gradient of the line through (1, 8) and (−1, 4).
items.e: Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x = (4 − 8) ÷ (−1 − 1) = −4 ÷ −2 = 2.

items.q: Find the gradient of the line through (3, −3) and (2, 0).
items.e: Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x = (0 − (−3)) ÷ (2 − 3) = 3 ÷ −1 = −3.
